talia: Flagging a weird onboarding crash in embed+rerank flow that looks related to SDK parity but with a different twist than the usual `vectors`/`embeddings` name issue.

mohit: quick summary?

talia: Repro on sampleapp: JS helper (v1.6.2) + Go backend (sampleapp using go-sdk v0.9.0). When pad_to_max=true the helper inserts a pad marker object into the embeddings array (e.g. `{"pad_marker": true}`) instead of a numeric vector. At the same time the JS helper serializes small floats in scientific notation (e.g. `1e-06`) while Go expects plain decimals. Net result: rerank zips arrays and then the scoring code tries to normalize vectors and chokes on the pad object and sci-notation strings.

greta: That's a new combination. Can you paste the minimal request + raw response we observed? (sanitized)

talia: Request: ```json
{
  "model": "open-embedding-small",
  "inputs": ["one", "two", "three"],
  "batcher": { "max_batch_size": 8, "pad_to_max": true },
  "pipeline": ["embed", "rerank"]
}
```

Raw response snippet: ```json
{
  "request_id": "r_pad_77",
  "status": "ok",
  "embedding_vectors": [ [0.12, 0.03, 0.004], {"pad_marker": true}, [1e-05, 0.002, 0.11] ],
  "candidates": [{"id":"one"}, {"id":"two"}, {"id":"three"}],
  "scores": [0.91, 0.05, 0.88]
}
```

oliver: So two different parity problems in one go: (A) field naming: some SDKs return `embedding_vectors`, others `embeddings` or `vectors` (B) pad signaling: instead of zero vectors we get a sentinel object `pad_marker` (C) numeric format: JS produced scientific notation strings for tiny floats and some Go parsing paths don't accept them as numbers.

mohit: Ops logs show auth refresh around the time too but this case repros even without auth races. The pad_marker originates in the batching helper pad code path where it wanted a cheap sentinel and inserted an object instead of a numeric zero vector. Later serialization step kept scientific notation for very small numbers, making some JSON parsers treat them as strings in certain SDK runtimes. The sampleapp normalization code did a strict typeof check and threw.

greta: Short-term mitigation we validated locally: set `batcher.pad_to_max=false` in onboarding template (no pad marker), and add a transform in sampleapp that coerces sci-notation strings to numbers and filters out `{pad_marker:true}` entries before zipping. Ugly but unblocks onboarding.

oliver: Proposed long-term fixes: normalize envelope to a canonical `embeddings` field (server accepts legacy aliases), ensure pad uses numeric 0.0 vectors (same length as model vector) not sentinel objects, and make SDK serializers always emit canonical decimal numbers (avoid handing down localized or stringified sci-notation). Also add an integration test that simulates pad_marker and rejects it.

mohit: I'll own adding a strict linter in the batching helper to forbid non-numeric pad tokens and to ensure pad vectors are the correct length and numeric. Greta, can you own a sampleapp hardening PR to coerce numeric strings and fail loudly with request_id when encountering unexpected pad objects?

greta: Yep. I'll add a pre-zip validation that: (1) rejects non-array embeddings, (2) coerces numeric strings to numbers with Number(), (3) filters and logs pad_marker with request_id and returns a clear error if counts mismatch. I'll add an integration test fixture in repos/sampleapp/examples/embed-precision-pad.

talia: I filed ticket DEVEX-5110 and attached the small repro. Ops: please note the temporary workaround in the onboarding README.

ops-bot: Action item: Update onboarding guide to recommend `batcher.pad_to_max=false` until patch lands.

mohit: Timeline: batching helper lint + pad fix targeted for next sprint; serializer normalization in JS SDK + server alias acceptance next week. I'll add a release note about rejecting sentinel pad objects.

oliver: One more small ask: make SDKs tolerant when parsing floats (accept both numeric and numeric-strings) but keep the stricter server-side invariant that pads are numeric vectors. That gives smoother rollback paths if a client hasn't updated.

greta: Will do. Thanks everyone 60a
